summary: The creation-time setup notification is dispatched fire-and-forget (async, not awaited), so channel-delivery latency never slows job creation; creation stays fast/silent. Part A adds no new work on the hot path (recovery-string generation only, on the already-denied branch). Part C is prompt text (no runtime cost). The only added I/O is one host getJobById + one markJobSetupNotified on the async notify path, which reuses existing infrastructure. No new synchronous or per-run overhead.
